contentEn:
Garage renovation in Vancouver costs $30 to $150 per square foot for basic improvements, and $80 to $300 per square foot for a full garage conversion into a habitable space such as a home gym, workshop, or secondary suite. A standard 400-square-foot single-car garage in Vancouver with new drywall, insulation, a garage door, and basic electrical typically costs $15,000–$40,000. Converting that same garage into a legal secondary suite or accessory dwelling unit (ADU) in Vancouver typically costs $50,000–$120,000 when all permit, electrical, plumbing, fire separation, and insulation requirements are met. Reno Stars has been completing garage renovation and conversion projects across Vancouver, Burnaby, Richmond, and the North Shore since 2015, and Vancouver's specific zoning rules—which differ significantly across RS, RT, and RM zones—make garage renovation in the city uniquely complex compared to other Canadian municipalities.

Vancouver's garage regulations are governed by a combination of the Vancouver Zoning and Development By-law, the BC Building Code, and municipal amendments that reflect the city's housing density goals and heritage preservation priorities. The key distinction in Vancouver garage renovation is whether the garage is attached or detached, whether it is converting into habitable space, and which zoning district the property sits in. Vancouver's RS (Single-Family) zones allow one accessory building (including a garage) up to a maximum floor area of 35 square metres (377 square feet) or 50% of the principal building's floor area, whichever is less. RT zones (Two-Family) and RM zones (Multiple-Family) have different rules that may prohibit or restrict garage conversions to habitable space depending on the specific sub-zone and the property's existing density.

Do You Need a Permit for Garage Renovation in Vancouver?

Permit requirements for garage work in Vancouver depend on scope and zoning:

  • Replacing an existing garage door or resheathing an existing garage roof with no structural changes: no permit required in Vancouver.
  • Re-framing, re-roofing, or altering an existing garage structure: requires a building permit and possibly an engineering assessment if structural members are modified.
  • Building a new detached garage in Vancouver: requires a building permit, a site plan showing setbacks, and compliance with the Vancouver Zoning and Development By-law coverage limits.
  • Converting a garage into a habitable space (workshop, gym, ADU, secondary suite): requires a building permit, an electrical permit, possibly a plumbing permit, and compliance with BC Building Code for accessory dwelling units.
  • Adding a bathroom or kitchen to a converted garage: requires a plumbing permit and possibly a stormwater management plan depending on the scope of impervious surface change.
  • Installing a natural gas line to a garage for a heater, fireplace, or workshop equipment: requires a FortisBC gas permit and a licensed gas fitter.
  • Converting a garage into a legal secondary suite in Vancouver: requires a building permit, electrical permit, plumbing permit, and compliance with the Vancouver Zoning and Development By-law secondary suite regulations including minimum ceiling height (1.95m), separate entrance, and egress requirements.
  • In flood-prone areas of Vancouver (such as the Fraser River flood plain zones), garage conversions to habitable space may be prohibited or require additional flood mitigation measures.

For any garage renovation that adds plumbing, electrical, or converts the structure to habitable space, a building permit is required in Vancouver. Reno Stars handles all permit applications and coordinates inspections as part of our standard project management service.

Garage Renovation Costs in Vancouver (2026)

Garage renovation costs in Vancouver are driven by the scope of work, the condition of the existing structure, and whether the project involves converting the garage to habitable space.

Basic Garage Renovation (No Conversion)

  • Garage door replacement (steel, insulated): $1,500–$4,500 per door
  • Roof replacement (asphalt shingles, det. garage): $3,000–$8,000
  • Exterior re-siding (vinyl, fiber cement): $4–$12 per square foot
  • New drywall interior (with insulation): $5–$10 per square foot
  • Electrical panel upgrade or sub-panel for garage: $2,500–$6,000
  • Epoxy floor coating or concrete sealer: $3–$8 per square foot
  • Basic lighting and outlet wiring: $1,500–$4,000

A basic 400-square-foot Vancouver garage renovation—roof replacement, new garage door, interior drywall, basic electrical, and floor coating—typically costs $18,000–$45,000.

Garage Conversion to Habitable Space

  • Structural reinforcement (if converting garage door wall): $5,000–$15,000
  • Full insulation to BC Building Code R-20 wall, R-40 ceiling: $3–$7 per square foot
  • Drywall and finishing: $5–$12 per square foot
  • Separate electrical panel or sub-panel: $3,000–$8,000
  • Plumbing for bathroom or kitchenette: $8,000–$25,000
  • Fire separation and rated drywall (one-hour fire wall to house): $3,000–$8,000
  • Separate entrance construction: $5,000–$18,000
  • Egress window installation (foundation wall): $3,000–$8,000 per window
  • HVAC extension or independent heating system: $4,000–$12,000
  • BC Building Code compliance and permits: $2,500–$8,000

A complete garage-to-habitable-space conversion in Vancouver (400 sq ft) typically costs $50,000–$120,000 depending on the level of fit-out and whether a bathroom is included. A garage-to-secondary-suite conversion adds $20,000–$40,000 on top of these figures due to the separate entrance requirement and higher BC Building Code requirements for dwelling units.

Detached Garage Construction (New Build)

  • New detached garage (wood frame, 400 sq ft): $25,000–$55,000
  • Concrete slab foundation (4-inch, garage-rated): $4,000–$10,000
  • Permits and inspections (City of Vancouver): $2,000–$6,000
  • Driveway apron connection to street: $3,000–$9,000
  • Stormwater management (if adding impervious surface): $2,000–$5,000
  • Electrical service to detached structure: $2,000–$5,000

A new 400-square-foot detached garage in Vancouver including permits, concrete slab, and basic electrical typically costs $40,000–$85,000. In areas with challenging soil conditions or high water tables (common in East Vancouver and the West Side), foundation costs can increase by 20–40%.

Vancouver Zoning Rules for Garages

The Vancouver Zoning and Development By-law sets specific rules for garage size, placement, and height that affect every garage renovation project in the city:

  • Maximum accessory building floor area in RS zones: 35 square metres (377 sq ft) or 50% of the principal building floor area, whichever is less—calculated on a formula that includes all accessory structures.
  • Maximum accessory building height in RS zones: 3.66 metres (12 feet) to the midpoint of a sloped roof, or 4.27 metres (14 feet) to the peak—these limits affect whether a loft storage or mezzanine is possible.
  • Garage setbacks in RS zones: minimum 0.9 metres (3 feet) from the rear property line and side property lines; cannot be in the required front yard or side yard on a flanking street.
  • Lot coverage limits in Vancouver RS zones: a maximum of 45% of the total lot area can be covered by all buildings including the house, garage, shed, and other structures—critical calculation when adding a new garage.
  • RT and RM zone garages: different rules apply depending on the specific sub-zone; some RT zones prohibit detached garages in rear yards, others allow them with conditions. A survey and zoning confirmation from the City of Vancouver is required before designing a new garage in an RT or RM zone.
  • Lane-access garage requirements: Vancouver lane-facing garages require a valid permit from the City of Vancouver Engineering Department in addition to the building permit, particularly for driveway crossings and lane modifications.
  • Heritage considerations: in Heritage Conservation Areas (including parts of Shaughnessy, Strathcona, and Kerrisdale), any exterior modifications to a garage visible from the street require a Heritage Heritage alteration permit.

Frequently Asked Questions About Garage Renovation in Vancouver

Can I convert my Vancouver garage into a legal secondary suite?

Yes, in most RS (Single-Family) zones in Vancouver you can convert an existing garage or construct a new garage with a secondary suite above it, subject to the Vancouver Zoning and Development By-law and BC Building Code requirements. The suite must be a minimum of 32 square metres (344 square feet), have a separate entrance, meet the 1.95-metre ceiling height requirement, have an egress window from each bedroom, and comply with fire separation requirements between the suite and the garage below. The property must also have adequate parking remaining (one parking space per secondary suite is required in most RS zones). In RT and RM zones, garage-to-suite conversions are subject to additional rules that vary by sub-zone. Reno Stars conducts a zoning confirmation with the City of Vancouver as part of every secondary suite feasibility assessment.

How close can I build a garage to my property line in Vancouver?

In Vancouver's RS zones, a detached garage must be a minimum of 0.9 metres (3 feet) from the rear and side property lines. The garage cannot be located in the required front yard or in the side yard on a flanking street. Additional restrictions apply for lane-accessed lots where the garage faces the lane: the City of Vancouver Engineering Department must approve the driveway approach and any modifications to the lane. For corner lots in Vancouver, the flanking street yard setback for an accessory building is typically 4.5 metres (15 feet) measured from the property line to the structure. These setbacks must be shown on a site plan submitted with the building permit application.

Does a garage renovation add value to my Vancouver property?

A professionally converted garage into a legal secondary suite in Vancouver typically adds 10–20% to a property's assessed value, according to BC Assessment data for the Lower Mainland. A completed secondary suite is a documented income asset and a significant factor in refinancing and resale valuations. A basic garage renovation (new door, roof, interior) without conversion adds 2–5% to assessed value primarily through improved condition. Converting a garage to a workshop or home gym without a suite conversion adds value primarily through buyer appeal rather than documented value increase. Unpermitted garage conversions—particularly those that create a rental unit without City of Vancouver approval—carry legal, insurance, and disclosure risks that can reduce effective property value.

What are the BC Building Code requirements for a garage conversion in Vancouver?

The BC Building Code requires that any garage converted to habitable space in Vancouver must meet the same standards as a conventional dwelling unit, including minimum ceiling height of 1.95 metres throughout the habitable area, adequate natural light via windows totalling at least 10% of the floor area, egress windows meeting minimum dimensions (0.35 square metres clear opening, minimum 15 inches in each dimension) from each bedroom, and a one-hour fire-rated separation between the converted garage and any adjacent living space in the main house. If the garage conversion creates a secondary suite, additional requirements include a minimum floor area of 32 square metres for a one-bedroom suite, a separate HVAC system or independent zone, hard-wired interconnected smoke and carbon monoxide alarms per BC Building Code, and a 100-amp minimum electrical service to the suite.

温哥华车库装修基本改善费用为每平方英尺$30至$150，将车库改建为 habitable space（如家庭健身房、工作室或套房）费用为每平方英尺$80至$300。温哥华典型400平方英尺单车库进行干墙、保温、车库门和基本电气装修，典型费用为$15,000至$40,000。将同一车库改建为合法套房或附属住宅单元（ADU），满足所有许可证、电气、管道、防火隔断和保温要求，典型费用为$50,000至$120,000。聚星装修自2015年以来一直在温哥华、本拿比、列治文及北岸完成车库装修和改建项目，而温哥华特定的分区规则——在RS、RT和RM区域之间差异显著——使温哥华的车库装修比加拿大其他市镇复杂得多。

温哥华的车库法规由《温哥华分区和开发附例》、卑诗省建筑规范及反映该市住房密度目标和遗产保护优先级的市政修正案共同管理。温哥华车库装修中的关键区别在于车库是附属还是独立、是否改建为有人居住的空间，以及物业位于哪个分区。温哥华的RS（独立屋）区域允许一个附属建筑（包括车库），最大楼层面积为35平方米（377平方英尺）或主建筑楼层面积的50%，以较小者为准。RT区域（双户）和RM区域（多户）有不同的规则，可能根据具体子区域和物业现有密度禁止或限制车库改建为有人居住的空间。

温哥华车库装修需要许可证吗？

温哥华车库工程的许可证要求取决于范围和分区：

  • 更换现有车库门或在无结构变更的情况下重新铺设现有车库屋顶：在温哥华无需许可证。
  • 重新框架、更换屋顶或更改现有车库结构：需要建筑许可证，如果修改结构构件，可能还需要工程评估。
  • 在温哥华新建独立车库：需要建筑许可证、显示退让距离的场地平面图，并需符合《温哥华分区和开发附例》的覆盖率限制。
  • 将车库改建为有人居住的空间（工作室、健身房、ADU、套房）：需要建筑许可证、电气许可证，可能还需要管道许可证，并需符合附属住宅单元的卑诗省建筑规范。
  • 在改建车库中添加浴室或厨房：需要管道许可证，根据不透水表面变化的范围，可能还需要雨水管理计划。
  • 为车库安装燃气管道（用于加热器、壁炉或工作间设备）：需要FortisBC燃气许可证和持证燃气安装工。
  • 将车库改建为合法套房：在温哥华需要建筑许可证、电气许可证、管道许可证，并需符合《温哥华分区和开发附例》套房规定，包括最低天花板高度（1.95m）、独立入口和逃生要求。
  • 在洪水易发区域（如菲沙河泛滥平原区域），将车库改建为有人居住的空间可能被禁止或需要额外的防洪措施。

对于任何添加管道、电气或结构改建为有人居住空间的车库装修，都需要在温哥华办理建筑许可证。聚星装修作为标准项目管理服务的一部分处理所有许可证申请并协调检查。

温哥华车库装修费用（2026年）

温哥华车库装修费用由工程范围、现有结构状况以及项目是否涉及将车库改建为有人居住的空间决定。

基本车库装修（无改建）

  • 车库门更换（钢制、保温）：每扇$1,500至$4,500
  • 屋顶更换（沥青瓦，独立车库）：$3,000至$8,000
  • 外部重新覆面（乙烯基、纤维水泥）：每平方英尺$4至$12
  • 室内新干墙（含保温）：每平方英尺$5至$10
  • 电气配电箱升级或车库分电箱：$2,500至$6,000
  • 环氧地坪涂层或混凝土密封：每平方英尺$3至$8
  • 基本照明和插座布线：$1,500至$4,000

温哥华400平方英尺车库基本装修——屋顶更换、新车库门、室内干墙、基本电气和地板——典型费用为$18,000至$45,000。

车库改建为有人居住空间

  • 结构加固（如改建车库门墙）：$5,000至$15,000
  • 全面保温至卑诗省建筑规范R-20墙体、R-40天花板：每平方英尺$3至$7
  • 干墙和装修：每平方英尺$5至$12
  • 独立配电箱或分电箱：$3,000至$8,000
  • 浴室或小厨房管道：$8,000至$25,000
  • 防火隔断和耐火干墙（与房屋之间一小时耐火墙）：$3,000至$8,000
  • 独立入口建造：$5,000至$18,000
  • 逃生窗户安装（地基墙）：每扇$3,000至$8,000
  • 暖通空调延伸或独立供暖系统：$4,000至$12,000
  • 卑诗省建筑规范合规和许可证：$2,500至$8,000

温哥华将400平方英尺车库改建为有人居住空间，典型费用为$50,000至$120,000，取决于装修程度和是否包含浴室。将车库改建为套房还需额外增加$20,000至$40,000，因为需要独立入口和对住宅单元更高的卑诗省建筑规范要求。

独立车库建造（新建）

  • 新建独立车库（木框，400平方英尺）：$25,000至$55,000
  • 混凝土板基础（4英寸，车库承重等级）：$4,000至$10,000
  • 许可证和检查（温哥华市）：$2,000至$6,000
  • 车道入口与街道连接：$3,000至$9,000
  • 雨水管理（如增加不透水表面）：$2,000至$5,000
  • 电气服务至独立建筑：$2,000至$5,000

温哥华新建400平方英尺独立车库，含许可证、混凝土板和基本电气，典型费用为$40,000至$85,000。在土壤条件困难或地下水位高的地区（温哥华东区和西侧常见），地基成本可能增加20%至40%。

温哥华车库分区规则

《温哥华分区和开发附例》对车库的大小、位置和高度设置了具体规则，影响该市每个车库装修项目：

  • RS区域最大附属建筑楼层面积：35平方米（377平方英尺）或主建筑楼层面积的50%，以较小者为准——按包括所有附属结构在内的公式计算。
  • RS区域最大附属建筑高度：坡屋顶中点3.66米（12英尺），或坡屋顶顶点4.27米（14英尺）——这些限制影响是否可能建造阁楼储藏室或夹层。
  • RS区域车库退让距离：后院地界线至少0.9米（3英尺），侧院地界线至少0.9米（3英尺）；不得位于所需前院或侧临街人行道的退让范围内。
  • 温哥华RS区域覆盖率限制：所有建筑（房屋、车库、棚屋和其他结构）最多可覆盖总地块面积的45%——这是新增车库时的关键计算。
  • RT和RM区域车库：不同子区域适用不同规则；某些RT区域禁止在后院建独立车库，其他则允许但有条件。在RT或RM区域设计新车库前，需要从温哥华市进行分区确认和测量。
  • 巷道车库要求：温哥华面向巷道的车库除建筑许可证外，还需要温哥华市工程部的有效许可证，特别是对于车道交叉口和巷道修改。
  • 遗产考虑：在遗产保护区（包括Shaughnessy、Strathcona和Kerrisdale的部分地区），对从街道可见的车库外观进行任何修改都需要遗产改造许可证。

关于温哥华车库装修的常见问题

我可以把我的温哥华车库改建为合法套房吗？

可以，在温哥华大多数RS（独立屋）区域，您可以将现有车库改建或将新车库与套房结合建造，需遵守《温哥华分区和开发附例》和卑诗省建筑规范要求。套房必须至少32平方米（344平方英尺），有独立入口，满足1.95米的天花板高度要求，每间卧室有逃生窗户，并符合套房与下方车库之间的防火隔断要求。物业还必须保留足够的停车位（大多数RS区域每个套房需要一个停车位）。在RT和RM区域，车库改建套房需遵守因子区域而异的附加规则。聚星装修将温哥华市的分区确认作为每个套房可行性评估的标准部分。

我在温哥华可以将车库建得离我的地产线多近？

在温哥华的RS区域，独立车库必须与后院和侧院地界线至少保持0.9米（3英尺）的距离。车库不得位于所需前院或侧临街人行道的退让范围内。对于车库面向巷道的巷道通道地块，车库还需获得温哥华市工程部批准车道入口和任何巷道修改。对于转角地块，温哥华的规则是：附属建筑在侧临街人行道的退让通常为从地界线到结构物4.5米（15英尺）。这些退让必须显示在随建筑许可证申请提交的建筑平面图上。

车库装修能增加温哥华物业的价值吗？

据大温地区卑诗评估局的数据，温哥华专业完成的套房改建通常使物业评估价值增加10%至20%。完成的套房是一份有记录的收入资产，是重新贷款和转售估值中的重要因素。基本车库装修（新车库门、屋顶、室内）不进行改建，主要通过改善状况使评估价值增加2%至5%。将车库改建为工作间或家庭健身房而不改建套房，主要通过吸引购房者来增加价值，而非有记录的价值增加。未许可的车库改建——特别是创建出租单位而未经温哥华市批准的——带有法律、保险和披露风险，可能会降低物业的有效价值。

温哥华车库改建的卑诗省建筑规范要求是什么？

卑诗省建筑规范要求在温哥华将车库改建为有人居住的空间必须满足与传统住宅单元相同的标准，包括整个 habitable area 的最低天花板高度为1.95米，通过窗户提供充足自然采光，窗户总面积至少为地板面积的10%，每间卧室的逃生窗户满足最低尺寸要求（通透开口0.35平方米，最小15英寸的宽和高），以及改建车库与主屋任何相邻居住空间之间有一小时耐火隔断。如果车库改建创建了套房，附加要求包括单间卧室套房最小楼层面积为32平方米、独立的暖通空调系统或独立区域、按卑诗省建筑规范要求硬连线互联的烟雾和一氧化碳警报，以及套房最小100安培电气服务。
